title: Support for host aliases in ~/.ssh/config
description:
Currently, gert does not support git remote ssh URLS that reference aliases defined in `~/.ssh/config`. It would be nice if it were possible to support this, but it's also very possible to work around this limitation.

## Desired use case:

`~/.ssh/config` contains

```
Host: my-git-server
Hostname: git.mydomain.com
User: git
IdentityFile: my-git/id_ed25519
```

and `git remote -v` returns

```
origin  my-git-server:myself/myrepo.git (fetch)
origin  my-git-server:myself/myrepo.git (push)
```

Wishing for `gert::git_push()`, `gert::git_pull()`, etc. to work with this use case.

It may not be possible, or it may be very difficult to do this with the `libgit2` API, so a #wontfix response would be reasonable.

title: FR: Interface to set multivalued config variables
description:
`git_config_set()` and `git_config_global_set()` don't seem to support multivalue config variables.

For example, if we have a global config file containing the following lines:

```gitconfig
[safe]
        directory = rlang
        directory = httr2
```

Then we can't add `gert`, too:

```r
git_config_global_set("safe.directory", "gert")
#> Error in libgit2::git_config_set_string : 
#>   entry is not unique due to being a multivar
```

I suggest exposing the libgit2 API functions `git_config_set_multivar()` and `git_config_delete_multivar()` via a new function `git_config_set_multivar()` and a variant `get_config_global_set_multivar()`, which would have an interface something like this:

### Usage

`git_config_set_multivar(name, value, pattern = NULL, repo = ".")`

`git_config_global_set_multivar(name, value, pattern = NULL)`

### Arguments

* `name` - Name of the option to set
* `value` - Value to set. Coerced to a string. Use `NULL` to unset.
* `pattern` - A regex matching existing values to replace with the new `value`. The default, `NULL`, adds a new value.

### Value

A character vector containing the previous values of `name`.

gert and git do not agree on what order to read the config
description:
It looks like {gert} prioritizes config items from top to bottom, but command line git prioritizes bottom to top in the case of duplicate keys.

I have a situation where I want to use a different set of credentials for a project. I found the `IncludeIf` directive for `.gitconfig` files from https://nicknisi.com/posts/git-includeif/ and I applied it like so:

```sh
[user]
    name="Clark"
    email=clark@email.com

[credential]
    helper=/path/to/helper

# ... gitconfig stuff ...

[includeIf "gitdir:/path/to/project"]
  path = ~/.gitconfig-pat
```

and in my `~/.gitconfig-pat` I have it set up to use the GitHub credentials for "Bizarro" in which I provision a temporary PAT inside of an environmental variable called `BIZARRO_TOKEN` a la https://git-scm.com/docs/gitfaq#http-credentials-environment

```sh
[user]
    name="Bizarro"
    email=clark+bizarro@email.com

[credential]
    helper = '!f() {echo username=clark-is-not-bizarro && echo "password=${BIZARRO_TOKEN}"};f'
```

When I run git from `/path/to/project` in the command line, I can commit, push, and pull as "Bizarro", but if I open R and run {gert} from the same directory, I am recognized as "Clark".

If I move the `IncludeIf` statement to the top of the file, then {gert} will recognize "Bizarro", but git will recognise "Clark"

Thanks!

- Check out `my-branch`, install the package at `my-branch` into a specific `libpath`

title: rewrite possible on resets
description:
_cf_: https://github.com/r-lib/gert/pull/233


```
$ sed -n '54,58p' gert/R/rebase.R
#' Reset your repo to a previous state
#'
#' * `git_reset_hard()` reverts to a point in history
#' * `git_reset_soft()` uncommits changes, but keeps the chsange uncommited
#' * `git_reset_mixed()` performs a simple `git reset`.
$ 
```

proposed more technical rewrite

```
#' * `git_reset_hard()` resets the index and working tree
#' * `git_reset_soft()` does not touch the index file or the working tree
#' * `git_reset_mixed()` resets the index but not the working tree.
```

which corresponds to the actual git documentation as below

```
$ man git-reset | sed -n '38,50p'
           --soft
               Does not touch the index file or the working tree at all (but resets the head to <commit>, just like all modes do). This leaves all your changed
               files "Changes to be committed", as git status would put it.

           --mixed
               Resets the index but not the working tree (i.e., the changed files are preserved but not marked for commit) and reports what has not been updated.
               This is the default action.

               If -N is specified, removed paths are marked as intent-to-add (see git-add(1)).

           --hard
               Resets the index and working tree. Any changes to tracked files in the working tree since <commit> are discarded. Any untracked files or
               directories in the way of writing any tracked files are simply deleted.
$ 
```

title: Dynamic linking against newer libgit2 versions if available?
description:
### Scenario

- Ubuntu 20.04 with libgit 0.28.4 via APT
- Goal: support for `ed25519` SSH (which [seems to be supported since v1.2.0](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2/pull/5750))

### Issues

- R binary builds from RSPM always link against their bundled version
- When attempting a source install, one first needs to set `USE_SYSTEM_LIBGIT2=1` to suppress using a static version of libgit2 and actually link against a newer system install of libgit2 (which are then found automatically)
- Even if linked successfully against a newer `libgit2`, subsequent reinstalls (which sometimes happen unnoticed in the background) of {gert} will change the `libgit2` version again to an old one

Is there a way to get dynamic support for linking against newer libgit2 versions? Is this a feature to consider for {gert}? I.e. could {gert} try to detect newer libgit2 installations (compared to the bundled and static ones) in well-known directories (e.g. `/usr/local`) and try to link against them automatically?

title: Gitlab Support
description:
Hi I'm interested in contributing gitlab support for `gert` would you be open to this?
From my initial cursory assessment only 1 function needs modification `make_cred_cb` in `credentials.R` everything else seems to be only using core git functionality.

However the tests present more of a challenge as many depend on github repos on @jeroen's github to implement the same tests for gitlab would require a copy of the testing reop(s) on gitlab and presumably the development team would like these test repos in a group they control. I could just clone these to a gitlab remote of my own for testing and transfer the ownership.
`test-auth.R`, `test-clone.R`, `test-rebase.R`, & `test-remotes.R` appear to contain the affected tests.

For `make_cred_cb()` there is a question of how to handle the presence of a GITLAB_PAT & and GITHUB_PAT variable being set. Perhaps a warning and a default to github, with an injunction to unset the environment variable if you don't want to use the github PAT? In the case where only one is set I would assume default to the one that is set. I've prototyped this in my fork: https://github.com/RichardJActon/gert

This might help with issues #145, #174, and possibly also #111 which all involve gitlab

title: Add default option to return author date in `gert::git_log`
description:
`gert::git_log()` returns the commit date of the commit, not the author date of the commit.

title: Add depth argument to git_clone
description:
We would like to be able to specify a depth flag in the git_clone function, similar to this issue raised with the cli package here: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/1456. If possible, please add a depth argument to your git functions to allow users to specify how many versions are cloned.

This can be done in the command line like so:
gh repo clone [repo] [directory] -- --depth 1

Original:

```
function (url, path = NULL, branch = NULL, password = askpass,
ssh_key = NULL, bare = FALSE, mirror = FALSE, verbose = interactive())
{
stopifnot(is.character(url))
if (!length(path))
path <- file.path(getwd(), basename(url))
stopifnot(is.character(path))
stopifnot(is.null(branch) || is.character(branch))
verbose <- as.logical(verbose)
path <- normalizePath(path.expand(path), mustWork = FALSE)
host <- url_to_host(url)
key_cb <- make_key_cb(ssh_key, host = host, password = password)
cred_cb <- make_cred_cb(password = password, verbose = verbose)
repo <- .Call(R_git_repository_clone, url, path, branch,
key_cb, cred_cb, bare, mirror, verbose)
git_repo_path(repo)
}
```

Proposed:

```
function (url, path = NULL, branch = NULL, password = askpass,
ssh_key = NULL, bare = FALSE, mirror = FALSE, verbose = interactive(), depth = NULL)
{
stopifnot(is.character(url))
if (!length(path))
path <- file.path(getwd(), basename(url))
stopifnot(is.character(path))
stopifnot(is.null(branch) || is.character(branch))
verbose <- as.logical(verbose)
path <- normalizePath(path.expand(path), mustWork = FALSE)
host <- url_to_host(url)
key_cb <- make_key_cb(ssh_key, host = host, password = password)
cred_cb <- make_cred_cb(password = password, verbose = verbose)
depth <- if(depth != NULL){as.integer(depth)}
repo <- .Call(R_git_repository_clone, url, path, branch,
key_cb, cred_cb, bare, mirror, verbose, depth)
# would add line here that makes sense when depth is null
git_repo_path(repo)
}
```

usage:

```
git_clone(url = https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown.git, depth = 5)
```

title: Support for getting specified versions of submodules
description:
Thanks for the great library. I've been migrated to gert from git2r, hoping to get support for cloning repositories with submodules (reference git2r's [issue on recursive](https://github.com/ropensci/git2r/issues/271)).

If I call a `git_clone()` on a repository that has a submodule (tracking a specific commit in the submnodule), then follow that with a `get_submodule_fetch()` I end up with the submodule being at the HEAD state of the remote repository, rather than the commit string specified in the parent module. I currently work around this by doing the `git_clone()`, then the `git_submodule_fetch()` then shelling out to call `git submodule update --recursive --init`.

Is there a way to carry out this process entirely within `gert`? There's an enticing bit of code (not exported) [here](https://github.com/r-lib/gert/blob/a515651fe19c24acc13e6e8a32cf553a4fa7d8a5/R/submodules.R#L121-L126) suggesting it's been considered. Even better would be to get full `git clone --recursive` support on the initial `git_clone()` call. That last function doesn't pass through any extra arguments at the moment.

Appreciate the time!

title: Access token as string not working for enterprise Github and Gitlab
description:
https://github.com/r-lib/gert/blob/3d5e13b3ba75acdd32c7efe3457a90b7806f7106/R/fetch.R#L48

Calling 
```
gert::git_clone(
      url = "https://github.company.com/repo1", path = ".", password = "accessToken"
    )
```
does not work because the username is not provided to make_cred_cb (NA).
By changing https://github.com/r-lib/gert/blob/3d5e13b3ba75acdd32c7efe3457a90b7806f7106/R/credentials.R#L40 to `username <- "git"`, this works with on-premise GitHub.
However, it does not work with on-premise Gitlab, where it fails with:
```
Error in libgit2::git_clone : 
  server requires authentication that we do not support
```

`git2r::clone` supports both via `git2r::cred_token`.

title: USE_SYSTEM_LIBGIT2=true the default unless libgit2-dev* is not available
description:
@jan-glx wrote in https://github.com/r-lib/gert/issues/117#issuecomment-768266802:

> No. I was not aware gert is sideloading binaries. Does CRAN even allow this?

I thought about this too.  It's convenient but it might be considered anti-social and unsafe.  Here are a few problems with it:

* SECURITY: It downloads and runs http://r-lib.github.io/gert/get-libgit2-linux.sh over HTTP - not HTTPS
* SECURITY: Can the static library download URL (https://r-lib.github.io/gert/libgit2-1.1.0.x86_64_linux.tar.gz) be compromised
* SECURITY: What happens if https://r-lib.github.io/gert/libgit2-1.1.0.x86_64_linux.tar.gz stops being maintained and someone finds a security flaw in libgit2?  In contrast, here system libgit2 packages should be safer because this scenario is taken care of by big Linux distros
* STABILITY: What happens if https://r-lib.github.io/gert/libgit2-1.1.0.x86_64_linux.tar.gz is inaccessible or disappears? This depends on someone maintaining that download URL.  In contrast, CRAN is designed for a very long lifespan without relying on individual package maintainers
* OFFLINE: On systems without internet access that provide a local CRAN mirror (via `repos=file://...`), on-the-fly downloads from online sources during package installs will fail
 
# Suggestion

My proposal is to make `USE_SYSTEM_LIBGIT2=true` the default and only fall back to `USE_SYSTEM_LIBGIT2=` if there is no system libgit2-dev* available.

title: http://r-lib.github.io/gert/get-libgit2-linux.sh uses --no-echo from R (>= 4.0.0)
description:
Just an FYI.  I noticed that <http://r-lib.github.io/gert/get-libgit2-linux.sh> uses `--no-echo` in:

```sh
${R_HOME}/bin/R --no-echo -q -e "curl::curl_download('$URL','bundle.tar.gz')"
```

That CLI option was introduced in R 4.0.0.   In R (< 4.0.0) it'll produce a warning, which might be harmless but add clutter.

---

BTW, to be conservative, `${R_HOME}` should be quoted to handle spaces, e.g.
```sh
"${R_HOME}"/bin/R ...
```
or
```sh
"${R_HOME}/bin/R" ...
```
depending on personal preferences.  The same applies to `${PWD}`.

title: Change default branch on `git_init()` to main, or at least an argument to set default branch
description:
Hello,

Currently, the is no way to perform, at least with a single command, the equivalent of:

``` shell
git init -b main
```

This is already the [recommended way by GitHub](https://docs.github.com/en/free-pro-team@latest/github/importing-your-projects-to-github/adding-an-existing-project-to-github-using-the-command-line) to start a repo that is supposed to be forwarded to GitHub.

There is any plan to change the default branch initiated to `main` or at least give support to change the default on repo start?

title: Send messages to standard output in interactive sessions
description: After switching usethis to gert, I get many opportunities to compare and contrast the messaging from usethis and gert. In many places, I will probably ultimately use `verbose = FALSE` or other methods to suppress gert output. But it brings up a general point: it seems that users often don't read text that looks like an error, which is the case for the reddish orange output coming from gert here (and elsewhere). usethis runs all user messaging through `rlang::inform()` in order to get this behaviour introduced in rlang 0.4.2 (quoting from its NEWS file): `inform()` now prints messages to the standard output by default in interactive sessions. This makes them appear more like normal output in IDEs such as RStudio. In non-interactive sessions, messages are still printed to standard error to make it easy to redirect messages when running R scripts (#852). Would you ever consider doing same, either via rlang or by inlining similar logic?

title: Return values
description:
My current impression is that gert doesn't have a super strong convention (or much documentation around) what it returns.

The function that motivated me to open this issue is `git_merge()`:

https://github.com/r-lib/gert/blob/4cba93c41900865288ae0f5ffd2bc45e6a8408d4/R/merge.R#L29-L54

I have a function in usethis that checks if all commits on the current branch have been pulled or pushed (from/to some appropriate remote ref). Currently, if we aren't up-to-date, I exit with advice to pull or push. This `check_*()` is used at the start of many functions, to confirm we are starting in a clean state.

But I'm tempted to offer to do what's needed, i.e. to do the pull or push. But then, for the `check_*()` flow to really work, I need to know if my pull or push succeeded. If it has, the `check_*()` can return `TRUE` and flow continues in the caller. Otherwise, we'd stop.

In the case of `git_merge()`, the info I need is being emitted via `message()`, which is tough to work with programmatically.

I'm just putting this general idea on the radar for future thought.

title: Add `track` argument to `git_branch_create()`
description:
If you create and checkout a local branch with a remote branch as start point, that remote branch is also set as the upstream tracking branch:

```
jenny@2020-mbp susan $ git checkout -b toby origin/toby
Branch 'toby' set up to track remote branch 'toby' from 'origin'.
Switched to a new branch 'toby'

jenny@2020-mbp susan $ git branch -vv
  master ff9ad4f [origin/master] Add cherry
  test   26d70dd Add cherry
* toby   2d3df6e [origin/toby] Add durian
```

Maybe gert could offer the same service in `git_branch_create()`?

Relevant excerpt from `git branch` docs (<https://git-scm.com/docs/git-branch#_description>)

> When a local branch is started off a remote-tracking branch, Git sets up the branch (specifically the `branch.<name>.remote` and `branch.<name>.merge` configuration entries) so that `git pull` will appropriately merge from the remote-tracking branch. This behavior may be changed via the global `branch.autoSetupMerge` configuration flag. That setting can be overridden by using the `--track` and `--no-track` options, and changed later using `git branch --set-upstream-to`.

More specific details re: `-t / --track` options for `git branch` and `git checkout -b`:

<https://git-scm.com/docs/git-branch#Documentation/git-branch.txt--t>

> When creating a new branch, set up `branch.<name>.remote` and `branch.<name>.merge` configuration entries to mark the start-point branch as "upstream" from the new branch. This configuration will tell git to show the relationship between the two branches in `git status` and `git branch -v`. Furthermore, it directs `git pull` without arguments to pull from the upstream when the new branch is checked out. This behavior is the default when the start point is a remote-tracking branch.

title: Make git_remote_set_url() less permissive or smarter
description:
As discussed in Slack.

`git_remote_set_url()` "works" even if there is no pre-existing remote named `name`. It does add such a remote to `.git/config`. But it looks like this:

```
[remote "upstream"]
	url = git@github.com:cran/TailRank.git
```

However a properly configured remote looks like this (note the refspec):

```
[remote "upstream"]
	url = git@github.com:cran/TailRank.git
	fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/upstream/*
```

To add a new remote, you really need to call `git_remote_add()`.

This lack of refspec is a rather subtle misconfiguration and it's quite hard to figure out what you've done wrong from error messages you see when, e.g., merging and pushing.

I propose one of these solutions:

1. `git_remote_set_url()` errors if no remote named `name` exists. Recommend to call `git_remote_add()`?
2. `git_remote_set_url()` delegates to `git_remote_add()` if no remote named `name` exists.

title: Ahead / behind
description:
We discussed in Slack but I'll open a real issue.

It would be great to get something like `git2r::ahead_behind()`, which wraps libgit2's `git_graph_ahead_behind()`:

https://libgit2.org/libgit2/#HEAD/group/graph/git_graph_ahead_behind

Here's where it would drop in to an internal helper in usethis:

```
git_branch_compare <- function(branch = git_branch(), remref = NULL) {
  remref <- remref %||% git_branch_upstream(branch)
  gert::git_fetch(
    remote = remref_remote(remref),
    refspec = remref_branch(remref),
    repo = git_repo(),
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  # TODO: replace with something from gert
  out <- git2r::ahead_behind(
    git2r::revparse_single(repo = git2r_repo(), revision = branch),
    git2r::revparse_single(repo = git2r_repo(), revision = remref)
  )
  stats::setNames(as.list(out), nm = c("local_only", "remote_only"))
}
```

I have a few ideas for improvements on `git2r::ahead_behind()`. I'm not sure the name is very helpful and the return value is very spartan:

> An integer vector of length 2 with number of commits that the upstream commit is ahead and behind the local commit

This is from libgit2's docs, explaining what `ahead` and `behind` are (I think they have a wording problem? maybe delete "from" here):

|          |        |                                             |
|----------|--------|---------------------------------------------|
| size_t * | ahead  | number of unique from commits in `upstream` |
| size_t * | behind | number of unique from commits in `local`    |

I think it would be great if the return value was a named list (not 2 integers), where the names refer clearly back to the argument names used to identify the 2 refs (commits) being compared. This makes downstream code more self-explanatory, i.e. you can do `if (x$remote_only > 0) {...}` instead of if `if (x[2] > 0) {...}`.

Name-wise, I find "compare" or "comparison" more evocative than ahead/behind. And I also like thinking of the return values as the number of commits that are unique to one ref, as opposed to the ahead/behind imagery.

title: git_push() and git_fetch() should have a default remote
description:

Docs for `git push`: <https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push>

> When the command line does not specify where to push with the `<repository>` argument, `branch.*.remote configuration` for the current branch is consulted to determine where to push. If the configuration is missing, it defaults to `origin`.

Seems like `gert::git_push()` should match that as closely as possible. The existing check against `git_info()$remote` appears to implement the check against `branch.*.remote configuration` for the current branch.

https://github.com/r-lib/gert/blob/4fe319dc8260072c46c048f5f56b04aef3791763/R/fetch.R#L50-L53

But this guard feels too aggressive:

https://github.com/r-lib/gert/blob/4fe319dc8260072c46c048f5f56b04aef3791763/R/fetch.R#L55-L56

I think this should fall back to `origin`.

I'm about to post a reprex showing how `git_push()` insists on me specifying a remote, even in a case where `git push` in the shell succeeds (falling back to `origin`).

title: Need to clarify what git_commit_all() does about new (untracked) files
description:
Currently `git_commit_all()` does not address new, untracked files.

``` r
library(gert)
#> Linking to libgit2 v0.28.4, ssh support: YES
#> Global config: /Users/jenny/.gitconfig
#> Default user: Jenny Bryan <jenny.f.bryan@gmail.com>

r <- tempfile(pattern = "gert")
git_init(r)
#> [1] "/private/var/folders/yx/3p5dt4jj1019st0x90vhm9rr0000gn/T/RtmpZKRbiJ/gert97c33bf58c92/"

writeLines(letters[1:6], file.path(r, "alphabet.txt"))
git_status(repo = r)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   file         status staged
#> * <chr>        <chr>  <lgl> 
#> 1 alphabet.txt new    FALSE

# git_commit_all() does not work when there's only new files
git_commit_all("nope", repo = r)
#> Error in git_commit(message = message, author = author, committer = committer, : No staged files to commit. Run git_add() to select files.

git_add("alphabet.txt", repo = r)
#> <git repository>: /private/var/folders/yx/3p5dt4jj1019st0x90vhm9rr0000gn/T/RtmpZKRbiJ/gert97c33bf58c92[@NA]
git_commit("Start alphabet file", repo = r)
#> [1] "7ed57f6c53dfc2cba40ea2573fe540d1f5a01262"
git_status(repo = r)
#> # A tibble: 0 x 3
#> # … with 3 variables: file <chr>, status <chr>, staged <lgl>

writeLines(month.name[1:6], file.path(r, "months.txt"))
git_status(repo = r)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   file       status staged
#> * <chr>      <chr>  <lgl> 
#> 1 months.txt new    FALSE

# git_commit_all() does not work when there's only new files
# second demo, to prove this has nothing to do with an unborn branch or whatever
git_commit_all("nope", repo = r)
#> Error in git_commit(message = message, author = author, committer = committer, : No staged files to commit. Run git_add() to select files.

cat(letters[7:9], file = file.path(r, "alphabet.txt"), sep = "\n", append = TRUE)
git_status(repo = r)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 3
#>   file         status   staged
#> * <chr>        <chr>    <lgl> 
#> 1 alphabet.txt modified FALSE 
#> 2 months.txt   new      FALSE

# this picks up only the modification to the tracked file
git_commit_all("Add more letters", repo = r)
#> [1] "27f0f048fcd0a4358b239dc52d7fdc72bd07931f"

# the new file is still there, unstaged, untracked
git_status(repo = r)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   file       status staged
#> * <chr>      <chr>  <lgl> 
#> 1 months.txt new    FALSE

# cleanup
unlink(r, recursive = TRUE)
```

<sup>Created on 2020-06-02 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0.9001)</sup>

I suppose `git_commit_all()` is intended to emulate `git add -A && git commit -m "Your Message"` which *would* add new, untracked files?

@jeroen What do you want this function to do?

If current behaviour is intended, we should change the docs and maybe messaging.

Or we should change the behaviour to match `git add -A && git commit -m "Your Message"` and add & commit new, untracked, unignored files.

`git_commit_all()` fails when more than one file is modified
description:
With >= two modified files in the index, I get

```r
gert::git_commit_all("message")
Error in !stat$staged && stat$status %in% c("modified", "renamed", "typechange") : 
  'length(x) = 2 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
Backtrace:
```

due to having one of the following set in Renviron

```
## Supported since R (>= 3.4.0)
_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_CONDITION_=true

## Supported since R (>= 3.6.0)
_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_LOGIC2_=true

```

title: Usage inside and outside of RStudio
description:
Running certain functions that need the SSH keys like `gert::git_pull()` I get different outcomes based on whether I run them inside or outside of RStudio.

(The same applies for `git2r::pull()`)

Within RStudio everything works and it seems that RStudio is doing something behind the scenes to detect the SSH key / talk to the SSH-agent.

Within a plain R CLI session I get

```r
gert::git_pull()                                                 
Trying to authenticate 'git' using ssh-agent...
Error in git_fetch(info$remote, ..., repo = repo) : 
  libgit2 error in git_remote_fetch: error authenticating: failed connectin
g with agent (23)
```

Any idea what kind of initialization the CLI way might be missing out on?

macOS 10.15.4
